title: Scholarships — WhiteHouse College of Business & Technology
description: WhiteHouse College of Business & Technology — Kathmandu University affiliated BIT and B.Tech Ed IT programs in Jhapa, Nepal.

paras: WCBT offers a range of scholarships to recognize talent, support deserving students, and open doors for learners across Eastern Nepal.

blocks.heading: Up to 75% merit-based scholarships
paras: Outstanding students can significantly reduce tuition costs through our merit scholarship program. Need-based and special category awards are also available.

blocks.heading: Find the support that fits you
paras: From academic excellence to community impact, multiple pathways exist to help fund your education at WCBT.

groups.title: Merit Scholarship
text: Up to 75% tuition support for outstanding academic performers in entrance exams and prior studies.

groups.title: Need-Based Aid
text: Financial assistance for students demonstrating genuine economic need with supporting documentation.

groups.title: Women in Tech
text: Encouraging more women to pursue IT and education technology careers.

groups.title: Sports & Talent
text: Recognition for exceptional achievement in sports, arts, or community leadership.

groups.title: Rural Access Fund
text: Dedicated support for students from remote and underserved communities in Eastern Nepal.

blocks.heading: Rewarding academic excellence
paras: High performers in entrance examinations and prior academics may qualify for substantial tuition reductions. We believe talent should never be limited by cost.
bullets: Based on entrance exam scores and +2 results
Tiered awards from 25% to 75% tuition coverage
Renewable each semester with GPA requirements
Open to both BIT and B.Tech Ed IT applicants

blocks.heading: Support for deserving students
paras: Students facing financial hardship can apply for need-based grants. Our committee reviews each case individually with confidentiality and care.
bullets: Income and family circumstance documentation required
Partial tuition grants and installment flexibility
Priority for students from underserved regions
Combined with merit awards where applicable

blocks.heading: Scholarship application process
paras: Follow these steps after receiving your admission offer to be considered for financial aid.

groups.title: Receive admission offer
text: Scholarship consideration begins after you are offered a place in BIT or B.Tech Ed IT.

groups.title: Submit scholarship form
text: Complete the financial aid application with required supporting documents.

groups.title: Review committee
text: Applications are evaluated based on merit, need, and scholarship category criteria.

groups.title: Award notification
text: Successful applicants receive scholarship details before the enrollment deadline.

blocks.heading: Investing in student success
paras: Scholarships are part of WhiteHouse Education Foundation's mission to expand access to quality higher education.

groups.title: Transparent criteria
text: Clear eligibility guidelines published for every scholarship category.

groups.title: Student-first review
text: Applications evaluated fairly with respect for each student's circumstances.

groups.title: Renewal support
text: Ongoing guidance to help scholars maintain eligibility and academic progress.

groups.title: Growing fund
text: Annual expansion of scholarship pools through foundation and partner contributions.

blocks.heading: Scholarship questions
paras: Answers to the most common financial aid inquiries.

faqs.q: Can I apply for multiple scholarships?
faqs.a: Students may be considered for more than one category, but total aid is capped per institutional policy. The committee assigns the most suitable award.
Merit scholarships can cover up to 75% of tuition. Partial awards and need-based grants are also available depending on funds.
Most awards require maintaining a minimum GPA each semester and good academic standing to continue receiving support.
Submit your scholarship application alongside or immediately after accepting your admission offer, before the enrollment deadline.
